terms.name: Smart Translation
terms.location: Not a setting. Each controller-output Config has a Smart Translator for its game. The Manager dashboard flags one that is out of date.
terms.summary: XIM's per-game aim system for controller output. It knows how the game's aiming works and handles reticle speed for you.

definition.text: XIM's own aim system, made "to produce the best possible aim on consoles". Each game's Smart Translator understands that game's aiming system, including how fast the reticle moves.

citations.quote: XIM's proprietary Smart Translation system was created for this purpose: to produce the best possible aim on consoles.

Like all XIM gaming adapters, XIM MATRIX features Smart Translators that understand everything about a game's aiming system. This includes reticle velocity behavior so Velocity Calibration is not needed. However, there are scenarios where you may want to provide your own calibration.

explanation.text: It is a controller-output feature. Mouse-and-keyboard output Configs don't have Smart Translators, because they don't need them.

citations.quote: Unlike controller output Configs which have Smart Translators that handle all reticle velocity tasks, mouse output Configs do not since they aren't needed.

explanation.text: It only works correctly when the game's own aim settings are what it expects. Lining those up is called Game Settings synchronization.

citations.quote: XIM MATRIX's Smart Translation input system must be synchronized with your game's aim settings for correctness to ensure optimal precision aim.
To function correctly, Smart Translators require specific in-game settings.

explanation.text: Because it handles the game's own stick behavior, an Aiming Curve you make is the curve you get in game. It is not stacked on top of the game's curve.

citations.quote: Meaning, it's not applying aim curves on top of the game's existing curves (producing incorrect and unintuitive aim behavior like other input devices). Rather, the curves you author will be the aim response you experience in game.

guidance.text: When a game changes its aiming, XIM can update that game's Smart Translator. Manager then shows a warning icon. Recreate the Config to get the update.

citations.quote: Out-of-date Smart Translator: A game's Smart Translator can be updated if the game's aiming system changed. If that happens, you will be notified with a warning exclamation icon. Recreate the Config to update its translation.

guidance.text: If your cm/360 test is way off, XIM's checklist includes an out-of-date Smart Translator. A red "cm/360" label means the Config's translator doesn't support accurate cm/360 yet. XIM asks you to tell its staff.

citations.quote: Your Config's Smart Translator isn't out-of-date
Your Config supports it (you will see the "cm/360" label display in red if it doesn't). (Let XIM staff know and updating the Smart Translator will be prioritized)

statement.text: XIM's action engine for bindings: sequences of actions, from simple macros to recoil control. A separate feature from the Smart Translator.

citations.quote: Features our proprietary Smart Translator precision aim system and our Smart Actions advanced macro engine.
Smart Actions are a powerful feature that enables the composition of action sequences to accomplish many different input automation scenarios from simple to complex.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Velocity Calibration
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Your own calibration of reticle speed. Controller output normally skips it, because the Smart Translator already knows the game.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Firmware
notToBeConfusedWith.note: The MATRIX's own software, updated with the Firmware Flash Tool. An out-of-date Smart Translator is fixed by recreating the Config, which Manager flags.

terms.name: Game Settings
terms.summary: How you line up the game's own aim settings with your Config. There are three methods: Standard, Custom and Manual.

definition.text: XIM's Smart Translation must be synchronized with your game's aim settings to aim correctly. There are three ways to do it: Standard, Custom and Manual.

citations.quote: XIM MATRIX's Smart Translation input system must be synchronized with your game's aim settings for correctness to ensure optimal precision aim.
Game Settings support includes three different synchronization methods: Standard, Custom, and Manual.

explanation.text: It applies only to Configs that output as a controller.

citations.quote: These settings apply only to Configs that output as controller.

explanation.text: Standard: the game's sensitivity goes to maximum and your aim is set in the Config. Custom: you pick some in-game aim settings and copy them into the Config. Manual: an advanced option where you calibrate to your own in-game settings.

citations.quote: Sensitivity is set to maximum
Your aiming behavior is then set through your Config.
To use, copy your game's aim settings into your Config:

citations.quote: Failure to configure your game's required settings correctly will result in negative aiming performance and the inability to effectively share and use Configs from others.
Failure to configure your game's required settings correctly will result in negative aiming performance and the inability to effectively share and use Configs from others.

This is the default option for controller Configs when custom is available for the game.

notToBeConfusedWith.note: A smoothing mode. Unrelated to Standard sync.

terms.summary: Keep your own in-game aim settings (like sensitivity and FOV) and copy them into the Config. Only for games that support it.

terms.name: Output type
terms.location: Chosen when you create a Config ("choose your inputs and outputs"). The dashboard shows the current output and connection status.
terms.summary: What the MATRIX presents itself as to your console or PC: a controller, or a mouse and keyboard. Dialed covers controller output only.

definition.text: XIM MATRIX can present to your console or PC as a controller, or as a mouse and keyboard, or both.

citations.quote: XIM MATRIX can present to your console or PC as controller or mouse and keyboard (or both).

explanation.text: Controller output means the game uses its controller aim. Mouse-and-keyboard output means the game uses native mouse aim. Mouse-and-keyboard output is outside Dialed's scope.

citations.quote: Use controller output when you want your game to use controller aim. If you want your game's aiming method to be native mouse, use mouse and keyboard instead.

explanation.text: Xbox: the guide's Xbox setup says the output must be Controller (Xbox, PS4). A genuine Xbox controller, or an officially licensed wired third-party one, in USB Port 3 handles authentication.

citations.quote: Next, choose your inputs and outputs. For an Xbox Config, the output must be Controller (Xbox, PS4).

citations.quote: Standard XInput controller
Xbox controller (Xbox authentication controller required)

terms.name: Velocity Calibration
terms.location: Edit your Config (pencil icon). For controller output: scroll down, press the "...", then Reticle Velocity Calibration.
terms.summary: Teaches the MATRIX how fast the reticle moves in your game, by doing full turns. Required for mouse-and-keyboard output. For controller output it is an optional, advanced tool that XIM discourages.

definition.text: Velocity Calibration is only required for Mouse and Keyboard Output Configs. It teaches the MATRIX how the reticle behaves in your game.

citations.quote: Velocity Calibration is only required when using a Mouse and Keyboard Output Config. It is used to teach your XIM MATRIX how the reticle behaves in the game you are playing.

explanation.text: Controller output doesn't need it: the Smart Translator already knows how fast the game's reticle moves. You can still calibrate if you want to use different in-game values.

citations.quote: Like all XIM gaming adapters, XIM MATRIX features Smart Translators that understand everything about a game's aiming system. This includes reticle velocity behavior so Velocity Calibration is not needed. However, there are scenarios where you may want to provide your own calibration.

citations.quote: Horizontal and Vertical Sensitivity
Zoom (ADS) Sensitivity
Field of View (FoV)

citations.quote: There are four different types of velocity calibration: Hip X, Hip Y, ADS X, ADS Y. If your game doesn't have an ADS mode, then, it'll only be X and Y.

Vertical (Y) calibration is the same process as horizontal (X) calibration except you will start with your reticle pointing straight down (at your "feet") and end pointing straight up (at the "ceiling").

explanation.text: Once done, you only redo it if you change in-game settings that affect aim, such as sensitivity or FOV.

citations.quote: Once complete, you never have to perform this process again unless you change any in-game settings that affect aim behavior (such as aim sensitivity, FOV, etc.).

terms.name: Simulate Analog Behavior
terms.location: Under Mappings, press the "..." and select Behavior Simulation.
terms.summary: Makes the sticks and triggers the MATRIX sends look more like a human hand. Only for games whose entry in XIM's list requires it.

definition.text: Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) simulates natural human behavior patterns. It makes the sticks and triggers sent to your console or PC look more analog.

citations.quote: Simulate Analog Behavior (also called "SAB") is used to simulate natural human behavior patterns. It will make the sticks and triggers being sent to your console or PC appear more analog.

citations.quote: Simulate Analog Behavior is only available for Configs that output as controller.

explanation.text: It exists for games with extra input requirements. SAB plus XIM's checklist lets you play within those rules. XIM says the goal is to comply with a game's requirements, not to get around them.

citations.quote: Some games include additional input requirements that define how a controller can physically interact with the game. Using SAB and following this checklist of hardware and additional Config requirements will allow you to play within the game's rules.

It is not a goal of XIM to bypass or otherwise circumvent the input requirements of a game. Rather, its purpose is to provide features to allow you be compliant and play within the constraints of the game using the input devices of your choice.

citations.quote: By default, these values are 0%.

Restricts how fast the stick can move

terms.location: Your Config's aim settings. The dashboard shows which mode is active.
terms.summary: Hip and Aim Down Sight (ADS) can each have their own aim settings, if the game has an ADS mode.

definition.text: If your game has an Aim Down Sight mode, you can set Hip and Aim Down Sight aiming separately. Otherwise there is one set of aim settings.

citations.quote: If your game supports an Aim Down Sight mode, then, you'll be able to set both Hip and Aim Down Sight aiming independently. Otherwise, you'll have a single set of aim settings.

explanation.text: The MATRIX knows when you are in ADS from your Config's game roles.

citations.quote: Game roles are used to determine if your game has an Aim Down Sight mode.
Your XIM MATRIX needs to know when your game is firing and when it's in aiming down sight (ADS) mode in order to function correctly.

explanation.text: By default, ADS inherits all its settings from Hip.

citations.quote: Inherit All: Inherit all ADS settings from Hip (this is the default)

explanation.text: The dashboard shows which mode is active right now.

citations.quote: Beneath the box art is the current input (button or key being pressed) and the aiming mode that is active (Hip or Aiming Down Sight).

explanation.text: Bindings can also be limited to one mode with their Activation setting: Hip-only or ADS-only.

citations.quote: Hip-only: Binding is enabled only when hip aiming
ADS-only: Binding is enabled only when aiming down sight

guidance.text: Check that the MATRIX sees your ADS: it quickly flashes green when you enter ADS and yellow when you return to Hip.

citations.quote: When you enter Aim Down Sight, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash green.
When you return to Hip, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash yellow.

aimStyles.text: Hip and ADS split how you aim, not what you aim with. If you aim down sights with both a pulse rifle and a hand cannon, both use your ADS settings.

citations.quote: If your game supports an Aim Down Sight mode, then, you'll be able to set both Hip and Aim Down Sight aiming independently. Otherwise, you'll have a single set of aim settings.

aimStyles.reasoning: The official split is by aiming mode (Hip or Aim Down Sight). Nothing in it knows which weapon you hold, so two weapons fired in the same mode share one set of settings.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: In-game ADS sensitivity settings

terms.name: Aim Settings Inheritance
terms.summary: Decides which ADS settings copy Hip: all of them (the default), all except sensitivity, or none.

Sensitivity Only: Inherit all ADS settings from Hip except sensitivity
Inherit Nothing: Inherit no ADS settings from Hip

explanation.text: Inherit All (the default): ADS uses all of Hip's settings, sensitivity included.

citations.quote: Inherit All: Inherit all ADS settings from Hip (this is the default)

explanation.text: Sensitivity Only: ADS gets its own sensitivity. Every other ADS setting still comes from Hip.

citations.quote: Sensitivity Only: Inherit all ADS settings from Hip except sensitivity

explanation.text: Inherit Nothing: ADS has its own settings, fully separate from Hip.

citations.quote: Inherit Nothing: Inherit no ADS settings from Hip

guidance.text: The default is Inherit All.

citations.quote: Inherit All: Inherit all ADS settings from Hip (this is the default)

Inherit Nothing: Inherit no ADS settings from Hip

terms.name: ADS Activation Delay
terms.location: Press the "..." under Activation.
terms.summary: Makes the MATRIX wait before switching between Hip and ADS aim, to match games that zoom in over time.

definition.text: Some games move from Hip to ADS (and back) over time rather than instantly. This delay makes the MATRIX wait before switching its ADS aim mode on or off, to match the game.

citations.quote: When transitioning from Hip to ADS aim (and vice versa), some games transition over time (rather than immediately).
You can add a delay so that XIM MATRIX will wait to activate or deactivate ADS aim mode when you aim down sight to match your game's behavior.

explanation.text: Known games with transition times, like Call of Duty, get a delay automatically when their Configs are created.

citations.quote: Known games that have transition times by default (like Call of Duty) are automatically given a delay when their Configs are created.

citations.quote: You can also choose to Smooth ADS Transition to better blend the reticle's movement as it transitions to ADS aim over the specified period of time.

guidance.text: If the game lets you set its ADS transition to immediate, do that and remove any delay the Config added.

citations.quote: Modern shooters can have the ability to customize ADS transition times. If you can, change it to immediate and remove any delay automatically added in their Configs.

citations.quote: If you are unsure, simply keep the values at 1%.

When you return to Hip, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash yellow.

explanation.text: The default toggle is View + Menu on an Xbox gamepad, or [ + ] on a keyboard. While it is on, the MATRIX light breathes white.

citations.quote: View + Menu for Xbox gamepads
[ + ] for keyboards
Manager will let you know when you are in Navigate Mode and XIM MATRIX's light will be displaying a white breathing sequence.

explanation.text: On controller output, you choose simple controller bindings for it. Connected gamepads pass straight through.

citations.quote: If your XIM MATRIX is currently presenting as a controller, you can choose the set of simple bindings to map your devices to controller. Connected gamepads are automatically passthrough mapped.

explanation.text: Auto Navigate Mode turns it on when you use the gamepad in Port 3, and off when you use any other input device.

citations.quote: You can configure Navigate Mode to automatically activate if a Gamepad in Port 3 is in use by using the Gamepad Auto Activate setting.
Navigate Mode will deactivate automatically when any other connected input device is used.

guidance.text: By default, Config hotkeys only work while Navigate Mode is on. The Navigate Only Hotkey Mode setting controls this.

citations.quote: Hotkeys, by default, are only available if Navigate Mode is active. To change, configure Navigate Mode.
In addition, you can choose to only allow Config loading via hotkey if Navigate Mode is enabled by using the Navigate Only Hotkey Mode setting.

guidance.text: While in Navigate Mode, you can load the next and previous Configs with specific buttons.

citations.quote: You can also load next and previous Configs using specific buttons while in Navigate mode. Those buttons can be changed (or removed) as well.

guidance.text: With Mouse, Keyboard, Controller output on PC, toggle Navigate Mode to pass your mouse and keyboard through to the desktop.

citations.quote: Select this method so you can still use your connected mouse and keyboard on your desktop. Toggle Navigate Mode to pass them through.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Config
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Your game setups. Navigate Mode behaves like a Config but is only for non-game tasks.

terms.name: Maximum Turn Speed
terms.location: Not a setting: it is a limit built into the game. The MATRIX's red flash for it is one of the light notifications in the Config's "..." options.
terms.summary: The fastest a controller game lets you turn. Nothing can go past it. The MATRIX flashes red when you hit it.

definition.text: Every controller console shooter has a maximum turn speed the game cannot exceed. The limit also changes with aiming angle.

citations.quote: All controller console shooters are limited by a maximum turn speed that the game cannot exceed. This maximum turn speed limit actually differs depending on aiming angle.

explanation.text: With controller output, the MATRIX quickly flashes red when you hit the limit, so you can adjust.

citations.quote: If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.

explanation.text: Velocity Mapping decides how your top speed maps onto this limit. After changing it, you may see the red flash more often: you can't exceed the game's limit either way.

citations.quote: When customizing Velocity Mapping, your XIM MATRIX may notify that you've exceeded maximum turn speed more often. This is because no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game.

explanation.text: With Custom sync, your in-game settings change the maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: Custom in-game settings affects the maximum turn speed of the game.

explanation.text: Thumbstick aim sensitivity can be set as a percentage of the maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: Depending on the type of Config, thumbstick sensitivity may be set through your in-game aim ettings, or, specified as a percentage (%) of maximum turn speed split between X and Y.

guidance.text: If fast turns cap out and you see the red flash, you have hit the game's own limit. It is not a MATRIX fault; adjust your aim accordingly.

citations.quote: If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.

When customizing Velocity Mapping, your XIM MATRIX may notify that you've exceeded maximum turn speed more often. This is because no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game.

aimStyles.text: Matters most for fast snaps and big turns. Slow tracking and small corrections stay well below it.

citations.quote: All controller console shooters are limited by a maximum turn speed that the game cannot exceed. This maximum turn speed limit actually differs depending on aiming angle.

aimStyles.reasoning: The limit caps top speed only. Slow, small movements never reach it.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Limit (Velocity Mapping)
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A cap you set yourself that can't be exceeded. The game's maximum turn speed is fixed by the game.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Sensitivity
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Your chosen speed in cm/360. It can't push you past the game's limit.

terms.name: Light notifications
aliases: aim speed and mode light notifications
terms.location: Edit your Config and press the "..." in its identity section (additional options).
terms.summary: Quick flashes on the MATRIX while you play: green entering ADS, yellow back to Hip, red at the game's maximum turn speed.

definition.text: The MATRIX light tells you when you switch between Hip and ADS, so you know your game roles are set up correctly. On controller output, it also flashes red when you hit the game's maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX will notify you whenever you switch between Hip and Aim Down Sight (if your game is configured for both modes). This is done so that you can know that your Config's game roles are set up correctly.

If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.

explanation.text: A quick green flash means you entered ADS. A quick yellow flash means you are back to Hip.

citations.quote: When you enter Aim Down Sight, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash green.
When you return to Hip, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash yellow.

explanation.text: A quick red flash means you hit the game's maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.

guidance.text: You can switch these notifications off in the Config's additional options.

citations.quote: Press the "..." to view additional configuration options available. These include:
Disabling light aim speed and mode light notifications

guidance.text: Keep them on while you set up and tune. They are how you confirm the MATRIX sees your ADS, and how you spot turns hitting the game's limit.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX will notify you whenever you switch between Hip and Aim Down Sight (if your game is configured for both modes). This is done so that you can know that your Config's game roles are set up correctly.

If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.
Disabling light aim speed and mode light notifications

guidance.reasoning: XIM says the ADS flash lets you know your game roles are set up correctly, and the red flash lets you adjust when you hit the limit. Both only help if the notifications are on.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Warning Lights
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Repeated or unusual light sequences that signal a fault, like rapid purple blinking. A quick yellow flash is Hip; repeated yellow blinking is a lost authentication controller.

statement.text: The slow breathing light shows the loaded Config's color, and white while Navigate Mode is on. In Global Settings you can turn off the breathing animation and adjust the light's brightness.

citations.quote: The Config's name, game box art, game platform, and color you chose for it are displayed. The color is also displayed on your XIM MATRIX with a "breathing" light pattern.
Manager will let you know when you are in Navigate Mode and XIM MATRIX's light will be displaying a white breathing sequence.
You can also disable your XIM MATRIX light breathing animations and adjust the light's brightness.

terms.name: Warning Lights
terms.summary: Unusual light sequences that signal a problem, such as rapid purple blinking for timing errors.

definition.text: The MATRIX light shows its current state. Warning Lights are the light sequences you may not have seen before, and what they mean.

citations.quote: But sometimes you may run into light sequences that you've never seen before. This is what they mean:

explanation.text: Rapid purple blinking at random times: timing errors that may hurt performance. XIM reports timing that is off by even a millisecond.

citations.quote: Rapid purple blinking: If your XIM MATRIX is blinking like this at seemingly random times, it means there are timing errors detected that may result in non-optimal performance.
If timing is off (even by just a millisecond) you will be informed.

explanation.text: Repeated yellow blinking: the MATRIX lost contact with your authentication controller. Check its USB connection and restart the MATRIX.

citations.quote: Repeated yellow blinking: Your XIM MATRIX has lost communication with your authentication controller.
Check the USB connection to your controller (especially if it happened when picking up your authentication controller). Correct any problems and restart your XIM MATRIX.

explanation.text: Repeated red and yellow blinking: a power fault. A device drew too much power, so the MATRIX shut down its ports. Fully charge rechargeable devices first; peripherals with lots of LEDs can cause it too.

citations.quote: Repeated red and yellow blinking: A power fault has been detected.
Make sure all rechargeable devices connected are already fully charged before using with your XIM MATRIX. Peripherals with a lot of LEDs (such a keyboards) can be an issue as well.
This means too much power is being drawn by one (or more) of your connected USB devices and your XIM MATRIX shut down its ports to prevent damage to itself.

explanation.text: Repeated red, green and blue blinking at startup: one or more Configs are corrupted. They cannot be recovered; you need a factory reset with the flash tool and to rebuild them.

citations.quote: Repeated red, green, and blue blinking at startup: At startup, your XIM MATRIX will notify you if one or more of your Configs are corrupted.
Unfortunately you won't be able to recover your Configs in this case. You will need to factory reset your XIM MATRIX using the flash tool and rebuild them.

explanation.text: A solid white light means a crash. Yellow, cyan and purple blinking at startup means a hardware failure. Both are rare; XIM asks you to let them know.

citations.quote: Solid white light: If your XIM MATRIX is not responsive and is showing this type of light, it means there was a crash.
Repeated yellow, cyan, and purple blinking at startup: At startup, your XIM MATRIX does self-diagnostic hardware checks on itself.
Seeing this means there is a hardware failure. This notification is extremely rare. If you see it, please let us know.
This is rare, but, if it does happen, please let us know.

guidance.text: Seeing rapid purple blinking? Check for loose USB connections, faulty cables, hubs or other hardware.

citations.quote: Check for loose USB connections, faulty cables, hubs, or other hardware.

guidance.text: Configs can be corrupted if the MATRIX loses power while saving, or if you restore a Config backup using an older firmware.

citations.quote: Your Configs can be corrupted if your XIM MATRIX loses power while it is writing itself, or, if you restore a backup of your Configs using an older firmware.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Light notifications
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Quick green, yellow or red flashes during play are aim notifications (ADS and maximum turn speed), not faults.

terms.name: Mouse DPI
terms.location: Entered in your Config's aim settings. To measure it: in Manager, press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds and select Check DPI.
terms.summary: Your mouse's DPI, entered in the Config. It must match the mouse, or your cm/360 will be wrong.

definition.text: Accurate real-world units, like cm/360, need your mouse DPI set correctly in your Config. It must match your mouse.

citations.quote: Accurate real world units require your mouse DPI be set correctly in your Config. Make sure this value matches your mouse DPI.

explanation.text: If it is wrong, your mouse aim won't be accurate.

citations.quote: Your mouse DPI (dots-per-inch) is a very important value that is set in your Config. If it is wrong, your mouse aim won't be accurate.

explanation.text: Gaming mice don't always save settings on the device, so the MATRIX has tools to check the true DPI and polling rate.

citations.quote: Gaming mice can be complex devices where it's not always clear if settings are saved on-device. XIM MATRIX provides tools to check the true DPI and polling rate of your mouse.

guidance.text: Check DPI: put a ruler under the mouse, hold the mouse icon in Manager for 3 seconds, select Check DPI, move the mouse 1 inch horizontally, and read the value.

citations.quote: Place a ruler below your mouse (a ruler phone app works too)
Press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds
Select Check DPI
Move your mouse horizontally for 1 inch

guidance.text: It won't match exactly, but it should be in range. If it isn't, check that your DPI setting is really saving to the mouse.

citations.quote: Gaming mice use high resolution sensors, it's normal to not match your DPI exactly, but, it should be within the range. If it's not, verify that your DPI selection is saving correctly to your mouse.

guidance.text: If a cm/360 test is way off, the DPI is the first thing XIM says to check.

citations.quote: Make sure your mouse DPI is configured accurately

guidance.text: Only if you use SAB: set the mouse DPI between half and its maximum, and verify it.

citations.quote: Set your mouse DPI between half to its maximum value
SAB is dependent on your mouse DPI being correct.

guidance.caveat: Applies only when Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) is on. SAB is a controller-output feature for games with extra input requirements.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Sensitivity (cm/360)
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Your chosen aim speed. The DPI must be right for that cm/360 to be accurate.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Polling Rate
notToBeConfusedWith.note: How often the mouse reports, checked with Check Rate. A separate value from DPI.

terms.name: Polling Rate
terms.location: Set on the mouse itself. To check it: in Manager, press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds and select Check Rate. Tapping a device icon on the dashboard also shows it.
terms.summary: How often your mouse reports. Manager can show whether the mouse really reaches the rate you set.

definition.text: The rate you set on your mouse. Manager can show it, and its response rate tool counts the non-zero values your mouse actually sends each second. A mouse may not respond at the rate you set.

citations.quote: Click on one of the device icons to get more information about it (such as the polling rate of your mouse).
The response rate tool is measuring the count of non-zero values coming from your mouse every second.
Your mouse may not respond at the polling rate you set due to onboard memory setting issues or wireless interference.

explanation.text: Two common causes of a low rate: the setting not saving to the mouse, or wireless interference.

citations.quote: Your mouse may not respond at the polling rate you set due to onboard memory setting issues or wireless interference.

explanation.text: Wireless: an adapter in Port 1 sits close to the MATRIX's Bluetooth antenna. XIM recommends moving it away with a USB extension, or using Port 2.

citations.quote: XIM MATRIX's compact design means that wireless USB adapters plugged into Port 1 are physically close to it's onboard Bluetooth antenna.
To ensure optimal wireless performance, it's recommended your wireless USB mouse adapter be placed physically away from your XIM MATRIX by using a USB extension.
If that isn't possible in your setup, plug your wireless adapter directly into Port 2 instead.

guidance.text: Check Rate: hold the mouse icon in Manager for 3 seconds, select Check Rate, move the mouse in circles without stopping, and read the value.

citations.quote: Press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds
Select Check Rate
Move your mouse continuously in circles

guidance.text: If the value isn't close to your polling rate, check the rate is really saving to the mouse. For wireless mice, reduce interference.

citations.quote: Check to make sure your polling rate is actually saving to your mouse, or
For wireless mice, make adjustments in your environment to reduce interference

guidance.text: Check XIM's Hardware Compatibility List. Some mice are reported as not working, or only usable at certain polling rates.

citations.quote: Below is a list of USB hardware that users have reported to be not working.
Zaunkoenig M2K (usable at 1000hz or less)
citations.note: One example of a mouse listed as usable only at certain rates.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Response (smoothing)
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A Standard smoothing setting for fast aim. Not the mouse response rate.

statement.text: How fast the MATRIX updates your console or PC, set in the Config's output connection mode. The guide's SAB checklist says to keep it at Standard, the default. It is not your mouse's polling rate.

citations.quote: When configuring the output connection mode of your Config, you can choose how fast you want your XIM MATRIX to update your console. Keep this value at "Standard" (which is default).

statement.caveat: For what XIM Central's 2023 videos call the MATRIX's "polling rate", see the update rate in Dialed's foundation settings.

terms.name: Firmware
terms.location: See your version: press the vertical "..." and select About. Update with the XIM MATRIX Firmware Flash Tool on a Windows PC or Mac.
terms.summary: The MATRIX's own software. It updates often, and you flash it from a PC or Mac over USB.

definition.text: The MATRIX is updated often with new features and fixes. Even a new MATRIX may have out-of-date firmware.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX is frequently being updated with new features and fixes. Even a new XIM MATRIX may have firmware that is out of date.

explanation.text: You update it over USB from a Windows PC or a Mac, using the Firmware Flash Tool.

citations.quote: You will need access to a PC running Windows or a Mac. Your XIM MATRIX is upgraded over USB.
Here we have links for both XIM MATRIX Manager (which is used to configure your MATRIX), and the XIM MATRIX Firmware Flash Tool. You will want to click on the firmware tool link.

explanation.text: Hold the MATRIX button while plugging it in: it shows blue in programming mode, yellow while updating, then the rainbow startup when done.

citations.quote: While continuing to hold the button, plug in your XIM MATRIX into your PC or Mac.
Your XIM MATRIX will now display blue meaning it's in firmware programming mode.
As your XIM MATRIX is updating, it will display yellow. The flash tool will display update progress as well.
Upon completion your XIM MATRIX will restart and complete the flash process. Finally it will display the normal rainbow startup sequence. Your XIM MATRIX is now updated.

guidance.text: Update before troubleshooting if an update is available.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX is frequently being updated with new features and fixes. It is recommended that you upgrade if there is an update available before continuing troubleshooting.
Your XIM MATRIX is frequently being updated with new features and fixes. It is recommended that you upgrade if there is an update available before continuing troubleshooting.

guidance.text: XIM asks you to run its latest firmware, which has all the most recent fixes. At times an upgrade is required to keep using the MATRIX.

citations.quote: Please make sure you are running our latest firmware which will have all our most recent fixes.
You will be required at times to upgrade your XIM MATRIX in order to ensure its uninterrupted use.

guidance.text: Back up your MATRIX before updating.

citations.quote: It is always recommended to back up your XIM MATRIX before updating it.

guidance.text: Xbox: don't update your Xbox controller's firmware through the MATRIX. Update it while it is connected directly to the Xbox.

citations.quote: Do not update your Xbox controller's firmware through your XIM MATRIX. Only upgrade your Xbox controller while it's directly connected to your Xbox.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Smart Translator updates
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A game's aim translation. Manager flags an out-of-date one, and you recreate the Config to update it.

statement.text: The game support Manager downloads: a down-arrow icon appears when an update is available, and Global Settings can force a download. Separate from flashing firmware.

citations.quote: New Games Database Available: When updated game support is available for your XIM MATRIX, you will see a down arrow icon appear. Press it to download the database.
Manager notifies you of game updates. However, if you want to force a games database download, you can do that here.

terms.name: Aim Magnitude
terms.location: A Smart Action (Aim Control) that you add to a binding.
terms.summary: A Smart Action that moves the reticle at a set speed, in degrees per second. Used with Aim Angle, for example for recoil control.

definition.text: Moves the reticle at a set speed and blends with your own aim. Used for things like recoil control or auto-turn, together with Aim Angle.

citations.quote: Move reticle at specified speed. Seamlessly integrates with user aim. Use in scenarios such as recoil control or auto-turn. (Use with Aim Angle.)

explanation.text: Its speed is set in degrees per second (°/s).

citations.quote: Aim Magnitude Smart Action is set in degrees-per-second (°/s)

explanation.text: For the reticle, use Aim Magnitude rather than Right Stick Magnitude, which doesn't blend with aim.

citations.quote: This action does not integrate with aim. Use Aim Magnitude for reticle modification.

guidance.text: For recoil control, set its value to match your weapon. XIM's basic recoil control doesn't try to match the recoil pattern exactly.

citations.quote: Customize your aim magnitude action value to best match your weapon.
This is basic recoil control and isn't intended to match the recoil pattern exactly. For a complete solution, see Recoil Modeling.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Magnitude Quantization
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Snaps your reticle speed to set steps. An aim setting, not an action.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Aim Magnitude Variance
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Adds a slight random offset to this action's value.

statement.text: A Smart Action that sets the right stick's deflection directly, for example for radial menus. It doesn't blend with your aim.

citations.quote: Set right thumbstick deflection at specified value. Use in scenarios such as automatic radial menu selection. (Use with Right Stick Angle.)
This action does not integrate with aim. Use Aim Magnitude for reticle modification.

terms.name: Aim Angle
terms.location: A Smart Action (Aim Control) that you add to a binding.
terms.summary: A Smart Action that sets the direction the reticle moves. Used with Aim Magnitude, which sets the speed.

definition.text: Moves the reticle at a set angle and blends with your own aim. Used for things like recoil control or auto-turn, together with Aim Magnitude.

citations.quote: Move reticle at specified angle. Seamlessly integrates with user aim. Use in scenarios such as recoil control or auto-turn. (Use with Aim Magnitude.)

explanation.text: Aim Control actions add to your own aim rather than replacing it.

citations.quote: Actions used to augment reticle velocity that seamlessly combines with the gamer's aim. Used in a variety of scenarios including recoil control.

explanation.text: For the reticle, use Aim Angle rather than Right Stick Angle, which doesn't blend with aim.

citations.quote: This action does not integrate with aim. Use Aim Angle for reticle modification.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Angle Quantization
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Snaps the direction your reticle moves to set angles. An aim setting, not an action.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Aim Angle Variance
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Adds a slight random offset to this action's angle.

statement.text: A Smart Action that sets the right stick's angle directly, for example for radial menus. It doesn't blend with your aim.

citations.quote: Set right thumbstick angle at specified value. Use in scenarios such as automatic radial menu selection. (Use with Right Stick Magnitude.)
This action does not integrate with aim. Use Aim Angle for reticle modification.

terms.name: Behavior Variance
terms.location: Under Mappings, press the "..." and select Behavior Simulation. To turn it off for one binding, press the watch icon while editing it.
terms.summary: Adds small, human-like variation to Smart Action waits and aim actions. On by default for every binding.

definition.text: Behavior variance simulates natural human behavior patterns for specific Smart Actions.

citations.quote: Behavior variance is used to add simulate natural human behavior patterns for specific smart actions.

explanation.text: Wait Variance is a percentage above or below each Wait. XIM's example: 20% on a 150 ms wait gives a wait between 120 ms and 180 ms.

citations.quote: Wait Variance is a percentage of variance above or below the specified value.
For example, 20% for a 150ms wait time means, when run, the wait will be between 120ms and 180ms.

explanation.text: Aim Magnitude Variance is a percentage above or below the action's speed. Aim Angle Variance is an offset above or below the action's angle.

citations.quote: Aim Magnitude Variance is a percentage of variance above or below the specified value.
The Aim Angle Variance value is a variance offset above or below the specified value.

explanation.text: It affects Smart Actions (waits, and Aim Magnitude and Aim Angle actions), not your own mouse aim.

citations.quote: Behavior variance is used to add simulate natural human behavior patterns for specific smart actions.
Or, a recoil control sequence's Aim Magnitude and Angle actions will be slightly offset from the values you specified:

explanation.reasoning: The guide defines it for "specific smart actions" and its settings are Wait, Aim Magnitude and Aim Angle variance. None of them names mouse, thumbstick or gyro aim.

guidance.text: It is on by default and set per binding. Press the watch icon while editing a binding to turn it off; the icon turns red.

citations.quote: Variance is controlled per-binding and is enabled by default.
To disable variance per-binding, edit your Config and press the watch icon.
The icon will turn red when it's off.

guidance.text: Setting a variance value to 0 turns that type of variance off for all bindings.

citations.quote: For all variance settings, setting to 0 will disable it for all bindings.

guidance.text: Turning off Wait Variance makes timing perfect, but less human.

citations.quote: While disabling wait variance will make your sequence timing perfect, it also means it will behave less human.

guidance.text: Turning off variance on a binding also turns off Simulate Analog Behavior for that binding.

citations.quote: When disabling Variance for a binding, this will also disable Simulate Analog Behavior for that binding as well.

guidance.text: Only if you use SAB: keep Wait Variance and Aim Variance on, and don't disable variance on bindings.

citations.quote: Wait Variance in on
Aim Variance is on
Do not disable variance on bindings

guidance.caveat: Applies only when Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) is on. SAB is a controller-output feature for games with extra input requirements.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Simulate Analog Behavior
notToBeConfusedWith.note: In the same Behavior Simulation menu, but shapes the stick and trigger output instead of Smart Action values.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Magnitude and Angle Quantization
notToBeConfusedWith.note: "Magnitude" and "Angle" here mean Smart Action values. Quantization snaps your own aim.

statement.text: An idea from earlier XIM devices: Configs within a Config. On the MATRIX, Smart Actions and groups replace most of it, and the Config loading actions can jump to another Config and back. See Load Config.

citations.quote: Prior XIM devices had the concept of sub-Configs which can be thought of Configs within your Config.

While a majority of the benefit of sub-Configs have been replaced by Smart Actions and groups, it can still be useful to quickly jump to a Config and back ("chaining") if there are significant changes in gameplay that occur that justify it.
Use the config loading actions for this.

statement.text: The guide uses this name once, on its Rumble Triggers page. It appears to mean Rumble Triggers; the guide has no separate setting by that name.

citations.quote: Recoil Triggers are only supported when your XIM MATRIX outputs as a controller.

statement.reasoning: The sentence is a note in the Rumble Triggers introduction, right after the guide explains what Rumble Triggers are. No other page of the guide uses the name.
